analysis: Market context: We're starting from a fully cash position with $100K. The screened universe shows a mix of UPTREND/basing and MIXED/SIDEWAYS candidates — many quality businesses that corrected meaningfully from their 52-week highs and are now forming bases. The macro environment remains uncertain (tariff noise, rates), which argues for selective, concentrated entry rather than deploying full capital. Three setups stand out with both strong fundamental and technical cases: (1) MSFT — arguably the highest-quality business in the list, basing at 31% of 52w range, fwd P/E 21 with 18% rev growth and $37B FCF, well off -11% from SMA200 but stabilizing; (2) APP — exceptional unit economics (76.9% op margin, 212% ROE, 65.9% rev growth, PEG 1.31 on fwd basis), basing at 38% of range, -11% vs SMA200 offers mean-reversion upside; (3) V — elite network-effect moat, 67% op margins, 60% ROE, $20.8B FCF, basing at 31% of range with SMA200 only -3.8% away and trend stabilizing. All three use 1.75x ATR stops (4-9% range, well within 4-15% guard rails), position-sized so worst-case hit costs ~1-1.5% equity each. Combined portfolio heat ~3.7%. Remaining ~33% cash serves as optionality buffer. Candidates like DDOG (+15.9% above SMA50) and SNPS (+15.7%) are too extended for new entries. COIN has -22% revenue growth — thesis unclear. CI is interesting value but mixed trend and political healthcare risk. Cash is held deliberately; no position forcing.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $413 or better; accept fill up to $416. Ideal entry on any intraday pullback toward SMA50 (~$397). If market opens flat-to-up, enter at market open near current price.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: Microsoft is arguably the highest-quality business in the S&P 500 — $3T market cap, 46% operating margins, $37B FCF, 34% ROE, 18% revenue growth driven by Azure cloud and AI monetization. Fwd P/E of 21 is very reasonable for this growth profile (PEG 1.28). The Copilot/AI stack is multi-year secular tailwind. Technical: Basing at 31% of 52w range after correcting from $539 to a low of $356. Now +4.1% above SMA50 but SMA50 itself barely positive — still in early basing, not extended. SMA200 gap of -11% offers meaningful mean-reversion upside. Stop at 1.75x ATR ($11.59/share) = $393.68, which is ~4.9% below entry and just above recent support zone.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) stop at $393.68 hit; (2) Azure growth decelerates materially below 20% QoQ in next earnings; (3) stock rallies to $520+ and shows distribution (close below 20-day MA after extended run). Otherwise hold for LTCG if thesis intact past 12 months. Time stop: reassess if no progress in 6 months.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $465 or better; accept up to $472. Look for any intraday dip toward the $455-460 zone near SMA50 for optimal entry. Do not chase above $475.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: AppLovin has one of the most impressive P&L structures in tech — 76.9% operating margin, 65.9% revenue growth, 212% ROE, $2.7B FCF on a $157B market cap. Forward P/E of 22 with PEG of 1.31 is genuinely cheap for this growth trajectory. The AXON ad engine is pulling revenue from Meta/Google budgets in mobile gaming and expanding into e-commerce. Technical: After a massive run from $303 to $733, the stock has corrected ~36% and is basing at 38% of its 52w range. It is in UPTREND (basing) with SMA50 sloping +1.3%/month. SMA200 gap of -11% is the recovery runway. ATR of 4.8% reflects justified volatility for a high-growth name; stop at 1.75x ATR = $39.38 below entry gives $429.45, sitting just below recent consolidation support.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) stop at $429.45 hit; (2) AXON ad revenue share growth stalls or Meta/Google respond with competitive pricing; (3) stock retraces below the SMA50 on heavy volume after a rally. Partial trim at $560 (50% position) to lock gains while letting rest run toward $620. Time stop: reassess if no progress within 90 days.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $316 or better; accept up to $320. Ideal entry on any pullback toward the $312-315 zone (near SMA50). Visa is liquid enough for market order if needed.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: Visa is an elite, near-monopoly payment network with 67.3% operating margins, 60.3% ROE, $20.8B FCF, and 17.1% revenue growth — compounding quietly while macro noise distracts. Fwd P/E of 21.5 (PEG 1.67) is well within fair value for a business this durable. No credit risk, asset-light, global volumes structurally growing as cash converts to digital. Technical: Basing at 31% of 52w range ($295-$371), only -3.8% below SMA200 — meaning the trend damage is minimal and SMA200 recovery is near. SMA50 only -1.0% slope drag; stock is +2.4% above it. This is a tight, low-ATR base (2.4%) — exactly the controlled consolidation before a resumption. Stop at 1.75x ATR = $13.39 below entry at $305.41, right below key support.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) stop at $305.41 hit; (2) global consumer spending data shows sustained deterioration or cross-border transaction volumes contract meaningfully; (3) regulatory action on interchange fees accelerates. Target $365 aligns with prior 52w high resistance zone. If reached, trim 50% and reassess. Candidate for LTCG extension if thesis intact at 12 months.
